text:
Sam O'Reilly is seven games into his NHL career, and he already has a debate attached. Edmonton drafted him 32nd overall in 2024 and traded him to Tampa Bay for Isaac Howard, and this month Oilers Nation and The Hockey Writers both revisited the deal, the latter arguing the Oilers haven't gained anything from it. O'Reilly scored his first NHL goal on Nov. 17 against Washington.

He arrived on the back of 71 points in 56 OHL games for London last season and 8 points in 7 games for Canada at the World Juniors. So far he's playing 13:03 a night with 2 points and 19 hits, and his chances (1.2 expected goals) match his production. Seven games is far too few to judge him, which is why our talent range for him is wide: about 26 points over the full season, anywhere from 16 to 38. For context, forwards picked around him since 2005 scored a median 0.32 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.29.
headline: Sam O'Reilly, seven games in, carrying a trade's weight
